text: The project-page lightbox is hand-written on purpose. When prev/next arrows were added, we considered an off-the-shelf lightbox (PhotoSwipe, GLightbox) and rejected it: this is a Zola site with no package.json and no bundler, so a 30-50KB library would have meant introducing a JS toolchain to replace ~80 lines of working plain JS on a native <dialog>. If someone proposes a library again, the bar is that it must justify the toolchain, not just the feature.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Zola's built-in get_url(path=..., cachebust=true) was considered for cache busting and deliberately rejected. It appends a query string (/assets/style.css?h=<sha256>) rather than changing the filename. That is incompatible with the one-year immutable header on /assets/* in static/_headers, because the unhashed URL /assets/style.css would still resolve and would then be frozen in browsers for a year with no way to recover. cachebust.py exists instead so that no unhashed name is ever reachable under /assets/. Do not replace it with the Zola built-in without also removing the immutable header.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text:
Project URLs gained a short id (/projects/<code>/<slug>/) so that one day any slug can resolve to the right project, Stack Overflow style. That redirect is NOT built yet, and here is the research behind deferring it.

The site is on Cloudflare Pages (the static/_headers file is the giveaway). Pages reads a _redirects file, which can rewrite or redirect at the edge, so no server is needed. But a single wildcard rule cannot send a wrong slug to the right one: nothing in the request tells the rule what the current slug is, and the rule engine has no lookup table. Redirecting to the correct slug therefore needs one generated rule per project.

The blocker is that any rule containing * or :name counts as a 'dynamic' redirect, and Cloudflare Pages allows only 100 of those (2000 static, 2100 combined). One rule per project caps the site at 100 projects. Above that the only route is Cloudflare Bulk Redirects, which lives in the dashboard or API rather than in this repo, so it leaves the build.

Second trap: Cloudflare docs state redirects are always followed 'regardless of whether or not an asset matches the incoming request'. Project images are colocated, so they sit inside the project's URL directory. A rule of /projects/<code>/* would swallow them and serve HTML where a JPEG should be. A rule shaped /projects/<code>/:slug/ (one placeholder, trailing slash) does not match a bare filename and avoids this. The alternative is moving images off the /projects/ prefix.

Cheaper unlimited variant, if the 100 cap ever bites: one dynamic rule /projects/:code/:slug/ -> /projects/:code/ 301, plus a build-time stub page at /projects/<code>/ that meta-refreshes to the current slug. Costs two hops and the second is a meta refresh, which crawlers weight less than a 301.

Nothing linked to the site yet when the URLs changed, so no Zola aliases were added for the old /projects/<slug>/ URLs.

Image captions are a parallel list in front matter (extra.captions, same order as extra.images) rather than a TOML list of tables ([[extra.images]] with file/caption). The list of tables is the cleaner shape, but it changes the type of images, which forces edits at every images usage in the templates plus the hero/thumb derivation in import_projects.py. Parallel lists touch one loop in the importer and one loop in project.html, and both lists are appended in the same loop iteration so they cannot desync. Captions come from the extractor JSON ("caption" per attachment, absent on files written before extractor commit ebc7fac, read as empty string). Not shown on the hero image or the project card by decision, only in the gallery and the lightbox.
